instructions: Take the steak out of the fridge and pat it dry. Season both sides with 3/4 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Peel the shallots and slice them thin.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and soft.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the steak and cook for 5 minutes without moving it, until the underside is deep brown. Flip and cook the other side for 4 minutes. You're cooking it to 130°F in the middle for medium-rare, so if you have a thermometer, check there. No thermometer? Press the steak: it should feel springy, like the base of your thumb.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Add the vinegar, thyme, broth and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt to the shallots. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 4 minutes, until the shallots are very soft and most of the liquid is gone.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the remaining 1 tbsp butter and any juices from the cutting board. Take out the thyme sprigs.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a few drops more vinegar.
Slice the steak thin against the grain. Spoon the shallots over the top and serve with mashed potatoes or steamed green beans.
method_notes: No version with 20 or more ratings could be read, so this is a fallback. The lead is Eat Live Travel Write's bavette aux echalotes: shallots cooked golden in butter, then vinegar, thyme and stock, finished with cold butter. It makes the sauce in the steak's pan; here it goes in a second pan at the same time so the whole dinner stays near 30 minutes. Sized up from a 10 ounce skirt steak to a flank steak, which Margarita's International Recipes found better for bavette than skirt.
